title: sticky-burst-window-mismatch-causing-intermittent-tenant-429s
creator: Asha Patel
description: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private reported short-lived but high-volume 429 bursts during peak traffic windows. Symptoms include opaque 429 responses with X-Rate-Limit headers showing remaining=0 while dashboards show quota still available. The produced outage pattern is: after a leader node failover or autoscaler shift, certain tenants experience a stream of 429s for 30s-3min and then recover. This ticket captures investigation, mitigation, and the patch to prevent recurrence.
observed_impact: Service: generation endpoints returned 429 for ~20-120s for affected tenants
Affected: a mix of Hosted trial users and 3 Dedicated customers (non-prod load tests) and one Private deployment (customer-managed cluster)
User-visible: failed requests, client retries, and some downstream timeouts; spike in support escalations and SLO alerts
reproduction_steps: 1) Warm tenant with sustained qps to create non-zero burst tokens
2) Trigger leader failover (kill serving leader or simulate node preempt) or trigger autoscaler relocation
3) Immediately send concurrent requests that collectively exceed per-tenant burst allowance
4) Observe 429s for the next 30-180 seconds with tokens showing zero in response headers despite quota dashboard showing allowance
root_cause_summary: A mismatch in burst-window state between components: the rate limiter cache (in-memory) and the cross-node burst metadata (Redis) used different window boundaries after failover and applied dedup logic incorrectly. Two contributing factors: clock alignment assumptions in the in-process cache (rounded by seconds) vs Redis stored window IDs (microsecond precision), and a regression from change that attempted to optimize burst reconciliation by early-evicting stale leases. Combined, these produced 'sticky zero' state where a tenant's burst tokens were marked drained on followers even after Redis indicated availability.
detailed_root_cause_facts: Cache eviction PR #1224 introduced an early-evict path that did not update the redis version token on leader handoff
Leader->follower handoff path expects a redis lease refresh but code path short-circuited when queue depth > threshold
Clock skew between nodes (<=250ms) caused different window rounding and incorrect window_id comparisons leading to 'mismatched window' branch being taken more often under load
Private deployment had older rate-limiter config (refresh_interval=15s) exposing the race more often than hosted (refresh_interval=5s)
temporary_mitigations_applied: Rolled back early-evict optimization on runtime hosts in Hosted (reverted commit runtime/1234) — immediate reduction in incidents
Increased burst window tolerance on Dedicated pools and instructed Dedicated ops to increase per-tenant burst allowance by 20% as stopgap
For Private customer, provided a hotfix script to align refresh_interval and restart coordinator agents during off-peak window
Opened an incident Slack channel (#incident-ENG-20345) and notified oncall teams and affected customers with status and ETA
proposed_fix: 1) Canonicalize window_id generation to use service-wide monotonic window epoch and microsecond granularity; enforce via a single helper in rate-limiter module
2) Make burst state updates atomic using Redis CAS (WATCH/MULTI or a versioned hash) so leader handoff always writes a new version visible to followers
3) Remove short-circuit path in leader->follower handoff and add exponential backoff with jitter for lease refresh to avoid contention under load

4) Add defensive fallback: if in-memory cache disagrees with Redis by more than one window, prefer Redis but return a soft-limit (quota-warn) header instead of hard 429 for 10s to allow graceful recovery
5) Add feature flag to toggle the new reconciliation behavior per-deployment (hosted default ON, dedicated/private off until validated)
implementation_notes: Patch targets: rate_limiter/{cache,redis_lease}. Go + C bindings in runtime-host
Expected code changes ~220 LOC across 6 files plus tests
Include integration test that simulates leader handoff and concurrent requests verifying no 429s and window convergence
Add observability: metric 'burst_window_mismatch_events' and trace span for 'burst_reconcile' with tags {tenant, node_role}
rollout_plan: Canary deploy fix to 5% of hosted capacity during low-traffic window (UTC 02:00-04:00)
Run synthetic load for 30m with leader failover exercises in canary
If stable for 2 hours, progress to 50% then full rollout over 6 hours
Dedicated: schedule manual upgrade with customer ops assistance; start with one Dedicated cluster in staging
Private: provide patch bundle and migration guidance; require coordinated downtime window for older-managed clusters
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for window_id helper and CAS update logic
Integration test harness that runs leader failover and asserts zero persistent 429s
Load test: replicate customer pattern (burst + failover) at 2x observed QPS for 20 minutes
Security review: confirm Redis CAS use doesn't expose new attack surface
SLO smoke checks: latency and error budget monitored for 24h post-rollout
postmortem_actions: Document design rationale and debug checklist in Confluence (link in 'links')
Ship metric + dashboard for immediate detection of mismatch events and alerting thresholds
Add e2e scenario to periodic chaos testing that includes leader preemptions and burst traffic
Follow-up project to harmonize rate-limiter config defaults across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
